intro:
Scalp care + focused facial care

We clear the flakes and oil that have built up on the scalp, gently release a tight scalp, and then carry that same flow down through to the face.

※ Carried out after consultation and according to individual condition. · A three-session programme

Does any of this sound familiar?

  • you wash in the morning, and by the afternoon the crown is flat and greasy
  • white flakes fall on your shoulders, so you avoid dark clothes
  • your scalp itches and your hand goes to it without thinking
  • your scalp always feels tight, and firm when you press it
  • there seems to be more hair in the drain than there used to be
  • drying your hair feels like a chore, so you leave half-dry and go out
  • keeping up with your face is enough of a job — the scalp feels like too much

Everyone has one or two of these. But if such days keep going on, it may be a signal from the scalp.

What is happening on the scalp?

One. The scalp produces more oil than the face. The scalp is one of the places on the body where sebum is produced most readily. Add flakes, dust and shampoo that has not been fully rinsed out, and it soon feels congested.

Two. Hair also takes "time off". Hair repeats a cycle: growing, then pausing briefly, then resting before it falls. Losing roughly 50 to 100 hairs a day is therefore natural. If it is noticeably more than that, it is worth having it checked.

Three. The scalp is thicker than you might think. It is not a single visible layer of skin but a structure of five layers, and inside it there is a tough membrane that covers the skull like a cap. Feeling that your "head is tight" or that your "scalp is hard" can mean that the tightness reaches below the surface.

Four. And the face is continuous with the scalp. Cross the hairline from the forehead and you are on the scalp. There is no boundary; it is one continuous sheet. Caring for the face and leaving the scalp out means missing the very place that supports the face from above.

What makes our scalp care different

We do not stop at the scalp — we carry on to the face

This clinic has always worked with facial firmness, lines and skin tone. We look at forehead, hairline and scalp as one continuous flow and treat them in a single session. You do not need two separate appointments for scalp and face.

We look at the whole ageing body

Ours is a clinic built around anti-ageing care. At the consultation we do not ask about the scalp alone. We listen to how your skin has been and what concerns you most, and set the direction from there. If you wish, other programmes at the clinic can be discussed in the same appointment.

It starts, and continues, with consultation

Even within the same programme, scalp condition differs from person to person. An oily scalp and a dry scalp need different care, and different intensity. The session follows your individual condition after consultation, and if anything feels uncomfortable during it, please say so at any time.

Three sessions — how they run

  • ① Scalp deep cleansing — We start by clearing long-standing flakes and oil. Just as you would not skip cleansing and layer on make-up, the scalp needs to be settled first. Clean but not over-dried is the state we aim for.
  • ② Negative-pressure scalp release — The device lifts and releases the scalp repeatedly, as if drawing it up gently. It is close to the feeling of pinching the scalp lightly by hand. This step is for those whose scalp has felt tight and stiff. Intensity is adjusted to the condition of your scalp.
  • ③ If hair has begun to concern you — Hair is made in the scalp. This step is the process of keeping that place comfortable.
  • ④ Scalp nourishing ampoule — An ampoule is applied to the cleared scalp to finish. It replaces what has been taken away. The product used is decided after consultation, according to your scalp.
  • ⑤ Focused facial firmness care — Once the scalp is comfortable, the same flow comes down to the face. Facial skin is cared for intensively and its condition settled.
  • ⑥ Hydration · nourishment · soothing — Moisture and nourishment are added to the face and it is calmed down. Replenishing and settling is the basis of good care.
We want to say this in advance

Hair loss has many causes and types. Loss driven by heredity and hormones, sudden round patches caused by an immune problem, and temporary shedding after stress or childbirth are all different. In those cases, medical examination comes before care. This programme does not replace treatment for hair loss. If the change in your hair is marked, please mention it freely at the consultation. Recurring skin problems such as acne can also require medical treatment separately from care, and we check this with you at the consultation.

Order of care

  1. ConsultationWe ask about scalp and skin condition and what concerns you most at the moment, then set the direction.
  2. Clearing the scalpAccumulated flakes and oil are gently lifted away.
  3. Releasing the scalpNegative pressure releases a tightened scalp.
  4. Scalp ampouleMoisture and nourishment are replaced, finishing the scalp work.
  5. Facial careContinues into facial firmness care with hydration, nourishment and soothing.
  6. Home care guidanceWe show you what you can do at home until your next visit.

※ The programme runs to three sessions in total; the interval between them is set after consultation.

What to try at home

Scalp

  • Wash in the evening. If you tend to run warm, the morning is fine too.
  • A dry scalp: every two or three days. An oily scalp: daily.
  • Wash with lukewarm water (around 38°C), and comb through with a wide-toothed comb first to loosen tangles.
  • Dry your hair fully before going out. Leaving it damp makes inflammation more likely. Use the cool setting, following the direction of the hair.
  • However much it itches, do not scratch with your nails.

Face

  • Moisturiser and sunscreen are the basics. Keeping to just those two makes a difference.
  • Avoid hot water and saunas. Long washing also dries the skin.
  • Use a gentle cleanser; oily cosmetics can bring on breakouts.

For both scalp and face

  • Rest well and sleep well. Stress shows directly on the scalp and skin.
  • Do not skip meals or lose weight rapidly. Have plenty of water, vegetables and fruit.
  • It is better to stop smoking. The same goes for smoke breathed in beside you.
outro:
Frequently asked questions

Why treat the scalp and the face together?
Cross the hairline from the forehead and you are on the scalp. It is one continuous sheet with no boundary, and the changes — dryness, loss of firmness — appear across both. Having in one visit what would otherwise be two appointments is easier on your time and on you.
Does it hurt?
No. It is closer to the feeling of the scalp being pinched up lightly and released. Intensity is adjusted to your condition, so if anything is uncomfortable please say so during the session.
Are three sessions enough?
Scalp and skin differ from person to person. This programme is built as three sessions; how you continue afterwards is decided together at a consultation.
Will scalp care make my hair grow back?
To be honest with you: this programme is a process of clearing and maintaining the scalp environment. It cannot take the place of treatment for hair loss. Hair loss is approached entirely differently depending on the cause, and there are separate, medically established treatments for it. If the change in your hair is marked, it is far more useful to have your current state assessed at a medical consultation.
How many hairs a day is normal to lose?
Around 50 to 100 a day is generally natural. To check at home, you can collect and count the hairs you lose over three or four days.
Doesn't washing daily make hair fall out more?
No. Washing regularly is in fact the basis of scalp care. A dry scalp: every two or three days. An oily scalp: daily.
Can I colour or perm my hair?
Colouring and perming within reasonable limits are not understood to cause ongoing hair loss. It is still better not to do them often. We advise at the consultation on how soon after a session you can have them done.
Why does dandruff keep coming back?
Dandruff is recurrent by nature, so keeping the scalp consistently clean matters. Sometimes a dermatitis that appears only on the scalp looks like dandruff; in that case the aim is not to eliminate it entirely but to reduce it and manage it so that it does not return.
I have a breakout on my face at the moment — can I still come?
It depends on the condition. Where inflammation is severe or recurrent, medical examination comes before care. We check at the consultation and tell you honestly.
Can I go straight out afterwards?
Yes, that is fine. Do dry your hair completely before leaving, and please apply sunscreen to your face.

Please note

  • This programme is carried out after consultation and according to individual condition.
  • The content of this page is general information about scalp and skin. It does not replace individual diagnosis or treatment.
  • Results and satisfaction may differ according to scalp and skin condition, daily habits and any illnesses you live with.
  • Hair loss, seborrhoeic dermatitis and acne are conditions that require medical treatment. If they apply to you, we will advise you at the consultation.
